motion_base.note: Diane NOT speaking - lips closed and still for the whole clip. Generated with the locked CONFIG 1 prompt and negative prompt, byte-exact from docs/VIDEO_1_GENERATION_CONFIGS.md. Native 1920x1080. 1 of 4 draws passed QA; the other three failed on camera drift (0.24/0.60/0.63 vs gate 0.1) or a moving mouth.

driving_base.method: base2's 241 frames reordered into a continuous walk. Every output frame is a bit-exact copy; only the ORDER changes. ffmpeg only, $0.00.
driving_base.join_size: 0.738 vs base2's own max consecutive-frame step of 0.657
guarantees: no cut outside the 103 declared joins
no blink ever played in reverse
direction changes ~1.4 s apart - drifts rather than nods

lipsync.loop_mode_note: Never triggers: each driving window exceeds its audio.

split.method: Re-encoded at the cut; a stream copy snaps to the nearest keyframe and would desync the remuxed audio. Frame count rounded UP so video always covers the audio.
split.measured: frames and video_dur_s are ffprobe measurements of the delivered v4 asset on 2026-08-21, not values carried over from an earlier revision. video_start_s is the batch offset snapped DOWN to the 25 fps frame grid; align_err_ms is that snap (video_start_s - batch_start_s), always <= 0, so the cut never starts late.

audio.note: LatentSync's returned audio (aac 16 kHz) is DISCARDED; the locked 24 kHz -24.5 LUFS master is muxed with -c:a copy, then transcoded ONCE to AAC-LC 128k/24 kHz/mono for delivery. MP3-in-MP4 is signalled as mp4a.69, which WebKit refuses to decode, so the original delivery was silent on Safari and on every browser on iOS. Video stream is COPIED bit-for-bit; nothing was re-rendered and no paid step was repeated. Verified 2026-08-21: frame count, duration, 1920x1080/25 and audio onset all unchanged; loudness held within 0.1 LU.

delivery.native: NO upscaling anywhere - base2 is native 1920x1080

measured.mouth_cheek_reference: approved demo 0.85, prior v2 0.84 - lower is softer, which is the correct direction; the rejected demo-driven set inverted to 1.10 and read as pasted on
measured.head_rms_note: Below the prior v2 (2.08) and well below the approved demo (6.16). KNOWN LIMITATION: base2 was generated from the locked prompt, which asks her to hold still. Fixing this needs a new base generated with a movement-positive prompt (lips still closed), ~$0.50 per draw plus a segment regeneration.

revision.reason: v3 drove LatentSync from the approved demo's own footage, in which Diane is already speaking. Repainting a mouth over a moving mouth inverted the mouth/face sharpness to 1.10 and left her jaw following the demo's words - rejected on review. v4 drives from a purpose-made clip in which her lips are closed, which restores a clean mouth and returns delivery to native 1920x1080.

safari_audio_fix_2026_08_21.what: delivery audio re-containered from MP3 (mp4a.69) to AAC-LC (mp4a.40.2); +faststart added
safari_audio_fix_2026_08_21.why: WebKit does not decode MP3 inside MP4 — picture played, narration was silent on Safari/iOS

oversized_frame_fix.problem: Delivered v4 asset was 156 frames = 6.240 s of picture against 6.241 s of embedded audio: the video did not cover the audio, breaking locked pipeline rule 'trim UP one frame so video covers audio'. The lesson narration and captions already declared 6.28 s (157 frames).
oversized_frame_fix.fix: Extended to 157 frames = 6.280 s by cloning the delivered final frame once (ffmpeg tpad=stop_mode=clone:stop=1), re-encoded with the delivery pipeline's own settings (libx264 -preset slow -crf 18 -pix_fmt yuv420p, scale=1920:1080:flags=lanczos,setsar=1), then remuxed against the ORIGINAL audio with -c:a copy.
oversized_frame_fix.synthesised_frame_note: Frame 156 is a HOLD on frame 155, not footage LatentSync generated. It falls in the trailing silence after the last narrated word, with the mouth already closed. Measured PSNR of frame 156 against frame 155 is 62.4 dB.
oversized_frame_fix.retained_picture_note: Frames 0-155 are a second h264 generation of the delivered picture at 53.4 dB average PSNR - visually lossless, and far smaller than the 1.9 Mbps re-encode the Thinkific package applies to every segment. A container-level concat that would have kept those frames bit-exact was tested and REJECTED: it left a 120 ms frame-duration stall at the join and a 6.32 s container duration.
oversized_frame_fix.audio_stream_note: Byte-identical before and after. The locked 24 kHz / -24.5 LUFS master is carried through, per pipeline rule 4.
oversized_frame_fix.cost_note: ffmpeg only. The alternative - regenerating the segment through fal-ai/latentsync so the frame is genuine - was costed at ~$2.37 and not taken.
